weather_reasons: NWS rain chance reaches 56% through this evening
Phoenix NWS discussion contains a convective/monsoon signal

afd.text:
000
FXUS65 KPSR 131801
AFDPSR

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Phoenix AZ
1101 AM MST Fri Nov 13 2026

.UPDATE...Updated Aviation Discussion.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...

- An incoming weather system will begin to cool temperatures and 
increase rain chances today and Saturday.

- Sunday and Monday will be warm and dry before a series of weather 
disturbances will bring occasional rain chances and cooling 
temperatures back to the Desert Southwest by Tuesday.
  
&&

.SHORT TERM /TODAY THROUGH SATURDAY/... 
The short wave trough that will bring cooler and wetter weather to 
the Desert SW starting today is currently in the Eastern Pacific 
just off the southern CA coastline. This system will move quickly, 
passing through southern AZ and Northern Mexico over the course of 
today. PWATs will increase to near 200% of normal, which, in 
conjunction with the energy from the short wave troughing feature 
rain chances will also increase, with PoPs peaking (30-60%) this 
afternoon across south-central AZ, then into the eastern higher 
terrain heading into the evening hours. Most of the expected shower 
activity will remain relatively light, talking about a few 
hundredths to at most a tenth of an inch, a few isolated 
thunderstorms resulting in briefly heavier rainfall rates cannot be 
ruled out given that there will be a least a few hundredths J/KG of 
CAPE present. 

Behind the short wave just discussed is another short wave that will 
quickly move in from the northwest. However this next system will 
remain across northern AZ. This will lead to rain chances being 
mostly confined to the north with the lower deserts forecasted to be 
dry, while the higher terrain areas could squeeze out an additional 
0.05"-0.10" Saturday. 

Outside of rain chances, these systems will also being in cooler 
temperatures as H5 heights will drop between 564-567 dam on Friday 
and 570-573 dam on Saturday. Afternoon highs will be in the upper 
70s for Friday then as the first short wave passes temperatures will 
cool into the low 70s across south-central AZ while out west 
temperatures will remain in the mid to upper 70s. after the first 
system passes low temperatures will lag in response, resulting in 
morning lows in the mid to upper 50s starting Saturday morning. 

&&

.LONG TERM /SUNDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/... 
Sunday will be a down day for shower activity with a brief period of 
shortwave ridging and some slight dry air advection from the 
northwest. This will lead to considerably less clouds, virtually no 
rain chances and temperatures climbing back into the upper 70s by 
Monday. Models remain in good agreement that another northern 
Pacific waves will continue to be ejected southeastward toward the 
U.S. West Coast starting early next week. Currently models suggest 
the next potential system reaching the California coast early Monday 
before reaching our region Monday night into Tuesday, where 
additional rain chances will return to the forecast with NBM PoPs 
peaking between 50-80% in south-central AZ and the higher terrain 
areas, however this far out this may need to be adjusted based of 
how the track of this low progresses. By Wednesday models are 
pointing towards yet again another low system, however larger 
discrepancies between models are evident for this system. Due to 
this confidence is low for rain chances by mid to late next week as 
things are too inconsistent at this time. 

Despite if these next systems bring rain to the region or not, a 
more significant cooling trend can be counted on by the middle of 
the week as these series of weather systems move in from the 
northwest. They will likely usher in a cooler air mass with 
afternoon highs trending more towards the upper 60s to low 70s, the 
higher or lower end of this range largely being dependent on the 
depth and position of the systems. 

&&

.AVIATION...Updated at 1800Z.

South Central Arizona including KPHX, KIWA, KSDL, and KDVT:
A period of SHRA with CIGs falling 6-8K ft AGL this afternoon will
be the initial weather issue, then increased probabilities of CIGs
developing 4-6K ft AGL Saturday morning. Confidence is good that
wind speeds will continue to increase as directions veer from SE
to SSE/S. By mid afternoon, winds becoming 150v210 should precede
SHRA, gusty winds, and occasional cigs 6-8K ft AGL focused between
21Z-00Z, when SHRA is most likely to impact the terminals. There
is also a 10% chance of an embedded TS with the SHRA. Confidence
is good that winds will then return to an E/SE component after
sunset as SHRA exits the PHX vicinity, however CIGs redeveloping
in a 4-6K ft AGL range appears likely after sunrise Saturday
morning. Late Saturday morning into the afternoon, another round
of SHRA is likely to develop mainly to the north and east of the
terminals, over the foothills and Central AZ higher terrain.
Chances of SHRA (around 10%) are currently too low to mention in
the PHX TAF on Saturday.

Southeast California/Southwest Arizona including KIPL and KBLH:
Periods of gusty winds will be the main weather issue through
Saturday morning under occasional mid/upper level cloud decks.
West winds will prevail through the period at KIPL, while winds at
KBLH will vary between SSE and SW. Confidence is excellent that
speeds will increase with gusts 15-20 kts at KBLH and 20-30 kts at
KIPL developing by mid afternoon and lasting into at least the
early evening. 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
A more unsettled weather pattern will begin to develop starting 
today and is expected to persist well into next week as a series of 
weather disturbances moving through the region will bring occasional 
rain chances and cooler temperatures. Minimum humidity values will 
increase today to between 30-40%. These higher minimum humidity are 
expected to remain elevated through much of next week. Expect 
overall light winds today before increasing Friday through early 
Saturday, mainly across the western districts, with peak gusts 
mostly staying under 25-30 mph.

&&

.HYDROLOGY...
Gila: A Flood Warning remains in effect from Painted Rock Dam 
through the Dateland area through at least early next week due to 
water released from the dam. Water release levels have now risen to 
3000 cfs and are expected to remain at this release level through 
the next several days. This will have the potential to flood farm 
fields and low-water crossings along the river downstream from the 
dam.

&&

.PSR WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
AZ...None.
CA...None.
&&

$$

SHORT TERM...Ryan
LONG TERM...Ryan 
AVIATION...Whittock/18
FIRE WEATHER...Lojero/Ryan 
HYDROLOGY...Lojero
